fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: John Bunyan was an English preacher and writer. He was baptised at Elstow in 1628 and died in London in 1688. He was a nonconformist (a Protestant outside the Church of England). He spent about twelve years in prison because he would not stop preaching.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Bunyan for the dates and the allegory of The Pilgrim's Progress. Questions name Christian, Vanity Fair, and the two parts. The Holy War is the later allegory of 1682.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: John Dryden was the leading English poet, playwright, and critic after 1660. He was born at Aldwincle in 1631 and died in London in 1700. In 1668 he became Poet Laureate (the official court poet). He lost that post in 1688 and then lived by writing.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Dryden in Unit I (Drama), Unit II (Poetry), and Unit VIII (Literary Criticism). Questions test the years of his plays, satires, and Essay of Dramatic Poesy. They also test the four speakers in that essay.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: John Locke was an English philosopher and physician. He was born at Wrington in 1632 and died at Oates in 1704. He argued that knowledge begins in experience, not in ideas present at birth. His political books defend government by consent and freedom of worship.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET places Locke in Unit 4 (prose). Questions test the 1689 publication against title pages dated 1690. They also ask how the Essay explains the mind.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: John Wilmot, Earl of Rochester, was an English poet and court wit (a sharp joker at court). He was born at Ditchley in 1647 and died at Woodstock in 1680. He lived at the court of King Charles the Second. His short life was famous for wild behaviour and sharp satire.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET places him in Unit 2 (Poetry) with the Restoration. Questions may pair his name with Dryden among court figures. Know the satire against reason, and do not use 1660 as his birth year.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: Rochester lived 1647 to 1680. His satire on reason was in manuscript by 1674 and in print by 1679.

fields.value: Samuel Pepys was an English naval official and the great diarist of the Restoration. He was born in London in 1633 and died at Clapham in 1703. He kept a private diary from 1660 to 1669 in shorthand. The diary was not printed until 1825, long after his death.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
